analysis.subject: physics
analysis.pageCoverage: Page covers weight as a gravitational field force versus aerodynamic forces, Newton's inverse-square law, definition of g near Earth's surface, the relation W equals m times g, and altitude effect shown with an airplane example.

overview.headline: Weight as Earth's gravitational force on mass and how it changes with altitude

keyPoints.point: Weight is the force generated by Earth's gravitational attraction on an object.
keyPoints.quote: Weight is the force generated by the gravitational attraction of the earth on any object.

keyPoints.point: Weight is a field force that needs no contact, while aerodynamic lift and drag need contact with air.
keyPoints.quote: The gravitational force is a field force; the source of the force does not have to be in physical contact with the object to generate a force.

keyPoints.point: Gravitational force between two particles equals a universal constant times product of masses divided by the square of distance.
keyPoints.quote: The gravitational force, F, between two particles equals a universal constant, G, times the product of the mass of the particles, m1 and m2

keyPoints.point: Weight equals mass of an object times gravitational acceleration.
keyPoints.quote: The weight W, or gravitational force, is then just the mass of an object times the gravitational acceleration.

keyPoints.point: Weight decreases slightly with altitude, so an airplane weighing 10000 pounds at the surface weighs about 9965 pounds at 35000 feet.
keyPoints.quote: If the airplane weighs 10000 pounds on the surface of the earth, it weighs 9965 pounds at 35000 feet

keyTerms.gloss: Force generated by gravitational attraction of Earth on an object
keyTerms.quote: Weight is the force generated by the gravitational attraction of the earth on any object.

keyTerms.gloss: Field force that acts without physical contact between source and object
keyTerms.quote: The gravitational force is a field force; the source of the force does not have to be in physical contact with the object to generate a force.

keyTerms.gloss: Mechanical forces like lift and drag that require contact with air
keyTerms.quote: Weight is fundamentally different from the aerodynamic forces, lift and drag.

keyTerms.gloss: Fixed number G used in calculating gravitational attraction between masses
keyTerms.quote: The gravitational force, F, between two particles equals a universal constant, G, times the product of the mass of the particles, m1 and m2

keyTerms.gloss: Acceleration formed from Earth's mass and radius that links weight to mass
keyTerms.quote: to form the gravitational acceleration, g.
